title: The ADI Code of Practice
whatItIs: A voluntary code agreed between DVSA and the National Associations Strategic Partnership (NASP). ADIs who agree to follow it can show this on their registration.
keyFacts: Phones: never use one while driving or supervising a client's driving; only when parked safely and legally.
On or before the first lesson, make clients aware of the code and of your terms of business.
Check entitlement to drive and ability to read a number plate at the statutory distance: first lesson, then regularly.
Keep a record of the client's progress, including the number of lessons given.
Never cancel or rearrange a client's driving test without their knowledge and agreement.
Advertised pass rates shouldn't be open to misinterpretation: make clear how they're worked out.

visual.caption: The 4 sections of the current code

items.title: 1 Personal conduct
items.text: Be professional, comply with the law, keep clients safe and treat them with respect.

items.title: 2 Business dealings
items.text: Account for money paid, record progress, and advise clients when to apply for tests.

items.title: 3 Advertising
items.text: Clear, fair and not misleading; claims can be verified and meet the CAP codes.

items.title: 4 Conciliation
items.text: Deal with complaints promptly and aim for a speedy resolution.

a.label: Unhappy with business service
points: Then: local Citizens Advice for guidance

b.label: Unhappy with professional service
points: Then: the ADI Registrar at DVSA

onTheTest.question: Under the ADI code of practice, which of these should your terms of business include?
options: The procedure for making a complaint
The name of the client's examiner
onTheTest.why: Code section 2: terms of business should include your legal identity and contact details, lesson prices and durations, test car terms, cancellation and refund terms, and the complaints procedure.

onTheTest.question: Under the code of practice, when may an instructor use a mobile phone during a lesson?
options: Only when parked in a safe and legal place
onTheTest.why: Code section 1: instructors agree not to use mobile devices when driving or supervising a client's driving, and only when parked in a safe and legal place.

traps: The current code is voluntary. A new mandatory code is due between late 2026 and early 2027 (date to be confirmed).
Keeping the school car back for a test? Give enough notice so the client doesn't lose the test fee.
Don't publish in-car footage of driving tests without permission from DVSA and the client.
If the client asks, go with them on their test and listen to the debrief.
